newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government says no Tshisekedi arrest threat.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government says no Tshisekedi arrest threat.

text.p: Zaire's radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi will not face arrest on his return from France on Tuesday following government accusations that he verged on treason, a government spokesman said.
"We will not arrest him just like that. The judiciary must first deepen its inquiry," government spokesman Boguo Makeli told Reuters on Saturday.
Tshesekedi said in a radio interview on Friday after talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is recuperating from cancer surgery in France, he had a mandate to form a national unity government.
He called for dialogue to end a Tutsi-led revolt in the east.
The government responded by saying that his comments and the action of his Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UPDS) verged on complicity with the enemy.
Tshisekedi, appointed prime minister by a national conference in 1992 and shunted aside by Mobutu in 1993, has never accepted the 1994 appointment of part-Tutsi Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.

The Kengo government has accused Rwanda of backing the rebels and invading Zaire. Tshisedeki said the revolt was essentially an internal problem and that rebel leader Laurent Kabila, a veteran Mobutu foe, had a role to play in Zaire.
The rebels hold a string of towns in the east.
